claims.quote: Complete loss-of-function mutations in NaV1.1 cause severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy (SMEI or Dravet's Syndrome)

claims.object_text: severely impaired sodium currents and action potential firing in hippocampal GABAergic inhibitory neurons
claims.quote: Mice with loss-of-function mutations in NaV1.1 channels have severely impaired sodium currents and action potential firing in hippocampal GABAergic inhibitory neurons without detectable effect on the excitatory pyramidal neurons, which would cause hyperexcitability and contribute to seizures in SMEI

claims.object_text: sodium currents and action potential firing are also impaired in the GABAergic Purkinje neurons of the cerebellum
claims.quote: sodium currents and action potential firing are also impaired in the GABAergic Purkinje neurons of the cerebellum

claims.object_text: drug combinations that enhance GABAergic neurotransmission
claims.quote: thermally induced seizures in these mice can be prevented by drug combinations that enhance GABAergic neurotransmission
Generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus (GEFS+) is caused by missense mutations in NaV1.1 channels
Familial febrile seizures is caused by mild loss-of-function mutations in NaV1.1 channels
mutations in these channels are implicated in febrile seizures associated with vaccination

claims.object_text: impaired alternative splicing of the mRNA encoding these channels may predispose to febrile seizures
claims.quote: impaired alternative splicing of the mRNA encoding these channels may also predispose some children to febrile seizures
We propose a unified loss-of-function hypothesis for the spectrum of epilepsy syndromes caused by genetic changes in NaV1.1 channels
sodium channel blockers are used in therapy of epilepsy
